title: Assessment performance of large language models (LLMs) for standardized, semantically grounded evaluation of flap perfusion using polarized dermoscopic images
summary: We are investigating whether modern AI language models (“large language models”) can reliably assess the blood supply of microvascular tissue transplants (free flaps) in the head and neck region using standardized polarized dermoscopic photographs. After surgery, images from several predefined areas of the flap are taken at specific time points and evaluated by the AI using a fixed scoring scheme. The AI assessments are then compared with the clinicians’ evaluations and the actual clinical course to determine whether perfusion problems can be detected or predicted early. In a subset of patients, an additional reference skin area is photographed to test whether this comparison improves the AI’s predictive performance.
conditions: Postoperative perfusion monitoring of microvascular free flaps in head and neck reconstruction (early detection of perfusion impairment/free-flap complications after free tissue transfer).

interventions.name: Dermoscopy images of four flap regions (central, intermediate, peripheral, and one clinician-defined “critical” region) at predefined postoperative time points; perfusion assessment using an LLM-based standardized scoring system.
As in Arm A, plus acquisition of a reference region (contralateral skin at/near the donor site) at the same time points; LLM-based scoring incorporating the reference region.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Patients undergoing microvascular free flap reconstruction (myocutaneous/fasciocutaneous/osteomyocutaneous) with a skin paddle in the head and neck region.
- Planned postoperative perfusion monitoring at the study site with feasibility to obtain the scheduled dermoscopic image acquisitions at predefined time points.
-Written informed consent for study participation and pseudonymized image data acquisition/processing.
Exclusion criteria:
- No informed consent or withdrawal of consent / refusal to participate.
- Inability to provide informed consent / lack of legal capacity (without permissible proxy consent per ethics approval).
- Objection to scientific use of collected data/images.
- Severe microangiopathy or relevant skin disease at/near the donor site (reference region) substantially limiting comparability.
